senses.gloss:
पिक पिक, अस्, ई, m. f. (probably for स्पिक,
cf. Gr. σπίζ-ω), the Indian cuckoo, Cuculus Indicus;
[cf. Gr. σίττη for σπίττη or ψίττη, σίττακος,
ψίττακος, ψιττάκη, βίττακος; Lat. pîcus, pîca; Old
Germ. speh, speht.]
—पिक-बन्धु, उस्, m. ‘friend
of the cuckoo,’ the mango tree.
—पिक-बान्धव,
अस्, m. ‘friend of the cuckoo,’ the spring.
—पिक-
राग or पिक-वल्लभ, अस्, m. ‘cuckoo's favourite,’
the mango tree.
—पिक-वर, अस्, m. an excellent
cuckoo.
—पिकाक्ष (˚क-अक्ष), अस् or अम्, m. or
n. (?), ‘cuckoo's eye,’ a vegetable and perfume (com-
monly called रोचनी).
—पिकाङ्ग (˚क-अङ्˚), अस्, m. a
small bird, commonly called Cātakīya.
—पिकानन्द
(˚क-आन्˚), अस्, m. ‘cuckoo's joy,’ the spring.
—पिके-
क्षणा (˚क-ईक्˚), f. ‘having eyes like the cuckoo's,’
the plant Asteracantha Longifolia or Capparis Spinosa
(= कोकिलाक्ष).

पिक्क पिक्क, अस्, m. an elephant twenty
years old (= विक्क); a young elephant in general.

पिक्का पिक्का, f., Ved. a collection or string
of thirteen pearls weighing a Dharaṇa.
